what do seniors need to do before gradua.question: What do seniors need to do before graduation?

variants.answer:
Here are the key things Vista Ridge seniors (Class of 2027) need to do before graduation, based on the current info from the school:

- **Order your Cap & Gown:** This is required for graduation. Vista Ridge has partnered with Herff Jones. You’ll receive order info at the senior meeting, and only the Cap, Gown & Tassel Unit is required.
- **Fill out the FAFSA:** Completing the [FAFSA](https://studentaid.gov/) is a graduation requirement. It opens October 1st. Most Texas universities have a priority deadline of January 15th, but always check your specific school's deadlines.
- **Attend Senior Events:** There are several events leading up to graduation, including:
  - Senior Meeting (for ordering Cap & Gown)
  - Senior Panoramic Picture (March during Ranger Time)
  - Senior Awards (May, invitation only)
  - Senior SAIL (relax and hang out with classmates)
  - Prom (more details to come)
  - Senior Scramble (more details to come)
- **Complete All Obligations and Hours:** You must clear all obligations and hours to pick up your Cap & Gown.
- **Attend Graduation Practice and Clap Out:** Details will be provided in the spring.
- **Name Pronunciation Form:** In May, you’ll be asked to fill out a form to ensure your name is pronounced correctly at graduation.
- **Graduation Walks:** LISD organizes walks at elementary schools for graduates. Transportation must be provided by you/your family. See [this link](https://news.leanderisd.org/class-of-2026-senior-walks-schedule-announced/) for more info.
- **Google Account Transition:** After graduation (usually July), your school Google account will move to an alum account (firstname.lastnameXX@alum.leanderisd.org). The password stays the same, but the alum account is only active for one year after graduation. Download any files you wish to keep.
- **Project Graduation:** An event for seniors—details are available at [Project Graduation](https://sites.google.com/view/vistaridgeprojectgrad/home).

**Important:** Make sure any university application deadlines (especially for Early Action/Priority) are met—many Texas schools have October 15th as this deadline.

Let me know if you need more information about any specific step, or if you have other graduation questions! Good luck, Ranger!

where do i report an absence?.question: Where do I report an absence?

variants.answer:
To report a student absence at Vista Ridge High School:

- You can submit absence notes or medical documentation via email from the parent/guardian’s email address on file to **VRHSattendance@leanderisd.org**, or you may hand deliver documentation to the Attendance Office.
- Phone calls are not accepted.
- Absence notes should be received within two days after the student returns to school.
- Notes are welcome in English and Spanish.

If you need more information, you can refer to the [Absence for students](https://www.leanderisd.org/attendance) page. If you have specific questions, the Attendance Office is the best place to ask.

what clubs and organizations are offered.question: What clubs and organizations are offered?

variants.answer:
Vista Ridge High School offers a wide variety of clubs and organizations for students to join! Here are some examples based on the latest available information:

---

### STEM & Career-Focused Clubs

- **STEM Competition Club**: Prepares members for science and math competitions (USAPhO, USACO, USABO, etc.), and offers volunteering opportunities related to STEM exposure.
  - Sponsor: Vanessa Ramirez (vanessa.ramirez@leanderisd.org)
  - Meetings: Room 2623, B-Day Ranger Times

- **National Technical Honor Society**: Offers career-focused workshops, leadership programs, community service, and recognition events. Open to those enrolled in a CTE program.
  - Sponsor: Miguel Valenzuela (miguel.valenzuela@leanderisd.org)
  - Meetings: C407, during Ranger Time

### Medical & Health-Related Clubs

- **Students in Medicine**: Features mini-lessons on medical topics and lab experiences. Meeting days after school (TBA).
  - Sponsor: Jacob Hoffman (jacob.hoffman@leanderisd.org)

- **HOSA (Health Occupations Students of America)**: Provides information on competitions, volunteer hours, job shadowing, and med school experiences. Open to students in specific Biomed CTE courses.
  - Sponsors: Jesse Leake / Cori Crandus (jesseleake@leanderisd.org)
  - Meetings: Room 1802, 3rd/4th Wednesday of each month during Ranger Time

### Service & Leadership Clubs

- **Key Club**: Focuses on community service, character-building, and leadership skills.
  - Sponsor: Caitlyn Goodfellow (caitlyn.goodfellow@leanderisd.org)
  - Meetings: Lecture Hall/Library, Tuesdays

---

These are just a few of the clubs currently listed. For a complete and updated list (including arts, academic, cultural, and interest-based organizations), you can visit the [Clubs & Organizations](https://vrhs.leanderisd.org/campus_information/clubs) page.

If you’re interested in committees at the district level, you can also explore [Leander ISD Committees](https://www.leanderisd.org/committees).

Get involved and make the most of your time as a Vista Ridge Ranger!
